log.title: DrivingBench: frontier models drive a real car.
log.summary: Frontier LLMs are given control of the steering, accelerator, and brakes of a real Toyota Corolla (via a comma.ai openpilot device) then evaluated on a fixed cone course, one command at a time, with a human supervisor ready to brake. Each model gets up to 3 attempts in one continuous chat, with a reflection after each attempt. Best progress along the course: GPT-6 Astra=100% (finished in 5:22 on attempt 2, after reaching 49% on attempt 1), Claude Fable 5.1=45% (9% ➜ 10% ➜ 45%), Grok 4.6=11%, GPT-5.6 Sol=6%. GPT-6 Astra is the only model to complete the course. Countdown note: the jump between attempts within the same chat (49% ➜ 100% for GPT-6 Astra, 9% ➜ 45% for Claude Fable 5.1) is a small real-world signal of in-context adaptive learning from physical feedback, with no weight updates. log.title: Figure Helix 2.5: Zero-Shot 30-Home Generalization.
log.summary: The most advanced neural network Figure has built. Pretrained on Index (Figure’s global-scale dataset of human experience, generating ~35 minutes of new data every second), Helix 2.5 is the first humanoid system to achieve zero-shot whole-body autonomy across 30 unseen real homes with no data collection, fine-tuning, or adaptation in those environments. Three whole-body behaviors from a single foundation model: tidying living rooms (13-15 toys), folding towels, and making beds. Index pretraining alone increased zero-shot success from 9% to 56% (strict all-or-nothing grading). Used half the task-specific data of Helix 02 while expanding generalization scope 30x. Whole-body self-correction: the robot repositions, changes stance, and walks around obstacles to recover from errors. log.title: Claude Fable 5.1 surpasses human baseline on SimpleBench, the last known text-based benchmark where average humans outperformed frontier LLMs.
log.summary: SimpleBench (Oct/2024) tested spatio-temporal reasoning, social intelligence, and linguistic adversarial robustness (‘trick questions’) designed to resist pattern-matching. A nine-person unspecialized human baseline scored 83.7%. For nearly two years, every frontier model has fallen short. Now, Claude Fable 5.1 (Sep/2026) tops the leaderboard at 86.6% (AVG@5), ~3 points above the human baseline. AGI countdown note: With SimpleBench cleared, no public text-only benchmark remains where an average human reliably outperforms frontier models. The remaining gaps to 100% are in embodiment, adaptive learning, and sensory grounding.

log.title: ByteDance and Peking University introduce In-Place Test-Time Training (In-Place TTT).
log.summary: ‘The static “train then deploy” paradigm fundamentally limits Large Language Models (LLMs) from dynamically adapting their weights in response to continuous streams of new information… In-Place TTT treats the final projection matrix of the ubiquitous MLP blocks as its adaptable fast weights, enabling a “drop-in” enhancement for LLMs without costly retraining from scratch.’ While a significant architectural step for test-time adaptation, this method is a stepping stone rather than the definitive, generalized adaptive learning (online learning) breakthrough required to push the AGI countdown further.

log.title: Adaptive Learning: Google DeepMind ‘Nested Learning’ (HOPE).
log.summary: A major paradigm shift addressing static/frozen models. The new architecture introduces “Self-Modifying Titans… a novel sequence model that learns how to modify itself [and] its own update algorithm”. Unlike traditional models which are frozen after training, Nested Learning allows models to “continually learn/memorize” during inference (test-time training). The HOPE module creates a “Continuum Memory System” mimicking human neuroplasticity, outperforming Transformers and RetNet in language modeling and reasoning tasks.

log.title: Anthropic’s new life sciences lab reports Claude autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats, from a single prompt.
log.summary: ~950 Claude agents searched a DNA database for 21 hours, screening 200,000+ reverse transcriptases (RTs) down to 20 compelling candidates. One agent spotted an unnoticed repeat array beside an RT in a jumbo phage: ‘that’s a CRISPR-like … repeat array?!’ The new system, array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART), shares traits found only in a handful of programmable DNA-editing systems. Prof Feng Zhang (MIT, Broad Institute): ‘This is an exciting example of how AI agents can contribute to biological discovery.’

log.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra autonomously broke a long-unsolved German Army Enigma message (MVUEH, 10/Jul/1941).
log.summary: Asked only to try the unbroken messages on the Crypto Cellar Research site, the model picked the most promising target, linked it to a related Enigma message broken in 2017, used the repeated place name ‘ROSENOW ROSENOW’ as a crib, and wrote its own Enigma simulator and Bombe in Python and C++ to recover the key and plaintext. It succeeded despite transcription errors in the ciphertext, a key unlike any other that day, and a rare wheel turnover.

log.summary: In a video captioned ‘A beautiful surprise’ (16/Sep/2026), Shock produced speech from neural signals without any mouth movement or vocalization. The synthetic voice was rebuilt from pre-illness recordings to reproduce Shock’s original voice, which his wife Cheryl calls ‘Original Ken.’ Neuralink engineer Skyler Granatir: ‘We want to build a system that goes directly from the brain to voice in real time.’ The broader PRIME Study now has 21 enro

log.title: Figure AI’s Helix 2.5 enables a humanoid to enter 30 unseen homes and immediately perform whole-body tasks (tidying, folding towels, making beds) with zero prior data collection.
log.summary: A single foundation model pretrained on Index, Figure’s global-scale dataset of human behavior, increased zero-shot success from 9% to 56% while using half the task-specific data of its predecessor. Figure also reported the first human-to-humanoid robot transfer scaling law, with Index now generating ~35 minutes of new human experience every second.

log.title: Paradromics announces its wireless brain-computer interface enabled a paralysed patient to converse in real time, including when she simply imagined the words.
log.summary: The 68-year-old woman, the first patient in the Paradromics clinical trial, was implanted with the Connexus BCI system (400+ electrodes) at University of Michigan Health in June 2026. The wireless, self-contained device decoded attempted speech, whispered speech, and imagined speech into computer-generated voice output, allowing spontaneous phone conversations with her grandchildren. The system also distinguished distinct neural patterns for speaking, imagining speech, and listening.

log.title: Agility Robotics unveils Digit 5, with $300M+ in contracted orders from Amazon, Toyota, GXO, and Mercado Libre, and goes public at ~US$2.5B, the first pure-play humanoid robotics company listed in the US.
log.summary: The fifth-generation robot lifts 23kg, reaches 2.2m, runs ~20 hours per charge cycle (10:1 run-to-charge ratio), and is designed to work fence-free alongside humans using NVIDIA’s Halos for Robotics safety platform. Digit 4 previously became the first humanoid to pass an independent OSHA field safety evaluation on a customer production line, logging 65,000+ hours across nine sites. Early Digit 5 customer deployments planned for December 2026.

log.title: XPeng launches what it calls the world’s first automated production line for advanced general-purpose humanoid robots, using robots to mass-produce robots.

Claude outperformed 28 experienced human safety researchers (averaging 2.5 years in the field) within a mean of 6.4 hours, and providing human-guided research directions did not improve performance. In five hours it explored 297 candidate optimizations across fused MoE, FMHA, kernel scheduling, and communication, discarded those without measurable end-to-end gain (including several that passed microbenchmarks), and opened seven pull requests. The verified structure involved 64 interconnected data paths, with zero manual wiring errors. Samsung’s System LSI (~6,000 staff) is using AI to narrow the productivity gap with Qualcomm (~52,000 staff). Separately, Samsung’s memory division cut process design kit recalibration time by over 95%.

StairMed has raised over 1.1 billion yuan (US$163 million) from Alibaba and Tencent, completed China’s first clinical trial of a 256-channel invasive BMI in early 2026, and plans multi-centre registration trials targeting ~40 patients by year-end. Following expert review, additional testing, and clinical confirmation, physicians established diagnoses in cases where earlier specialist analysis had failed. Prof Tim Cernak (UMichigan): ‘The merger of high throughput experimentation and modern AI represents a new frontier of scientific discovery.’

Advisors including Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun.
